question: How can cell inclusion alter a low-dimensional velocity mapping while the high-dimensional velocity estimates remain fixed, and how does this differ from streamline display?

elements.role: High-dimensional per-cell RNA velocity estimates kept fixed for retained cells; not refitted after beta-cell exclusion.
Smoothed spliced-expression differences and expression-space UMAP have separate mapping roles; UMAP is not physical position or time.
Full and beta-cell-removed computational populations define different candidate relationships and recomputed transition probabilities.
Population-dependent mapping combines embedding displacements with transition weights; it is not direct display of original physical velocity.
The same53 pre-endocrine cells supply the directional comparison across both mappings; not106 independent samples.
Downstream interpolation and streamline visualization are distinct from per-cell estimates and mapped vectors.

transferable_rules: Separate upstream estimates, population-dependent mapping and downstream display; a fixed estimate can yield a different map after computational subset changes.
Name the shared comparison population and repeated-cell identity; do not double the sample size or generalize selected-region directions to every cell.
When printed signs, normalization or smoothing roles conflict, keep those conflicts visible and avoid introducing unsupported geometric guarantees.
